headline: Meta Ads Featured AI-Generated Child Abuse Imagery Approved by Platform
summary: Researchers found over 50 ads containing explicit AI-generated CSAM and images of minors alongside suggestive statements, which Meta has since removed.
details: Over the past nine months, Meta has run dozens of paid ads that included explicit AI-generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and images of minors alongside sexually suggestive statements. These ads, which reached thousands of accounts across the US, UK, and over a dozen European countries, were discovered by researchers at the Tech Transparency Project (TTP).

More than 50 image and video ads containing abusive content were found in Meta's ad library, with some linking to 'nudify' or 'undressing' apps. These ads were reviewed, approved, and allowed to run by Meta, with the company collecting ad revenue before they were eventually removed for violating policies.

One video ad used a thumbnail of a child with text stating 'Realizing Deep Fantasies with Generation AI.' Upon clicking, it played clips of adults in sexual acts and superimposed the child's face from the thumbnail onto the scene. Another ad repeatedly showed an image of a young girl in a sexual position with text saying, 'I can show you more.'

While many ads had minimal reach, at least one reached over 2,500 accounts in Europe. The ads were published between November last year and early August, and some were reportedly targeted specifically at men. Meta claims new AI technology has since been implemented to better detect and block violating ads at upload.

After WIRED contacted Meta, the company removed the ads from its library. A Meta spokesperson stated, 'Sexual exploitation is horrific, and we work aggressively to keep it off our platform.' They added that many ads predated new AI technology and that the company is constantly improving its detection systems.
